originalTitle: Trump envoy calls for Sudan-wide arms embargo as drone attacks escalate
title: A Big Idea to Help Our Friends in Sudan!
content:
Hello, Friends! It's Reporter Kiki!

Hi everyone! It's your friend, Reporter Kiki, here to share some news from our wonderful continent of Africa. I hope you are all having a super day, learning and playing. Today, we're going to talk about something happening in a country called Sudan. Sudan is a big and beautiful country right here in Africa, just like where you live! But sometimes, even in beautiful places, there can be some sad things happening.

What's Happening in Sudan?

Imagine you and your friends are playing outside. Now, imagine if some grown-ups in your town started to fight. That's a bit like what's happening in Sudan. There are some groups of people who are not getting along, and they are fighting. This fighting makes many people, especially children, very sad and scared. It means kids can't always go to school, or play safely outside, or even sleep soundly at night. That's not good, is it? This fighting is also happening with special flying robots called drones. Have you ever seen a toy drone fly? These are bigger and can be used for fighting. They fly high up in the sky. When people use drones for fighting, it can make the situation even more dangerous for everyone on the ground. Did you know? Drones are like robots that fly! Some are small and can take pictures, but big ones can be used in grown-up fights. It's much better when they are used to help people, like delivering medicine or taking cool photos of nature, not for fighting.

A Special Helper Wants to Help!

Because the fighting in Sudan is getting worse, a special helper from a big country far away called America came to visit. He saw what was happening. He works for the leader of America, and his job is to try and help countries have peace. When he saw the sad things happening in Sudan, he had a very important idea. He wants to help stop the fighting and make things safe for everyone, especially the children. He wants to help stop the fighting from getting even bigger. He knows that when people fight with weapons, it makes everything much, much worse. So, he thought of a big rule that could help. It's a bit like when your parents make a rule to keep you safe.

The 'No More Guns' Rule!

This special helper had a really big idea called a 'Sudan-wide arms embargo.' Now, that sounds like a very grown-up name, doesn't it? But let's break it down so it's super easy to understand! 'Arms' means weapons. Things like big guns, bombs, and even those fighting drones we talked about. 'Embargo' means to stop something. So, an 'arms embargo' means a rule to stop weapons from going into a place. And 'Sudan-wide' means this rule would be for the whole country of Sudan. So, the special helper wants a 'no more guns' rule for all of Sudan! He thinks that if fewer weapons go into Sudan, then people will have fewer things to fight with, and maybe, just maybe, the fighting will stop. Imagine if all the fighting toys were taken away; then you'd have to find a different way to play, right? A peaceful way! Did you know? The best way to solve a problem is to talk about it, not to fight! Talking helps everyone understand each other better and find a happy solution.

Who Decides This Big Rule?

Now, making a big 'no more guns' rule for a whole country isn't something one person can do alone. It needs many countries to agree. There's a very big club of countries from all over the world. It's called the United Nations, or the UN for short. The UN's main job is to try and keep the world safe and peaceful. They want all children, everywhere, to be happy and safe. Inside the UN, there's a special team called the Security Council. This team has countries that meet to talk about big problems, like fighting in Sudan. If they want to make a big rule, like the 'no more guns' rule for Sudan, they have to vote. Voting is when everyone says 'yes' or 'no' to an idea, and if most people say 'yes,' then the idea happens. So, the special helper wants this special team at the UN to vote 'yes' for the 'no more guns' rule for Sudan. Did you know? The United Nations has almost every country in the world as a member! They work together like a big family to help everyone get along and solve problems peacefully.

Not Everyone Agrees Yet

This is where it gets a little tricky, friends. Even though the special helper wants this 'no more guns' rule, not all the countries in the UN Security Council agree. There are two big countries, Russia and China, that say 'no' to making this rule for all of Sudan. They have their own reasons for saying 'no,' and it means that making this big rule is harder. It's like when you and your friends want to play a certain game, but one or two friends want to play something else. Sometimes it's hard for everyone to agree, even when it's about something important like peace. Their 'no' means that the UN Security Council might not be able to make this rule right now. But the special helper is still trying his best to talk to everyone and explain why he thinks it's so important for the children and families in Sudan.

Why Is This Important for Kids?

This news is important for kids like you because when there's fighting, children suffer the most. They can't learn, they can't play, and they can't feel safe in their own homes. Peace means children can go to school, play outside with their friends, eat yummy food, and sleep soundly at night without any fear. That's what every child deserves, everywhere in the world! Did you know? Every child has rights! One of those rights is to live in peace and safety, and to be protected from harm. This is why many people work hard to stop fighting in places like Sudan.

Let's Hope for Peace!

So, while the grown-ups are still talking and trying to agree on the 'no more guns' rule, we can all hope for the best. We hope that all the people in Sudan can find a way to talk instead of fight, and that peace will come very soon. Because peace is the most important thing for everyone to grow up happy and strong. Thank you for listening, friends! This is Reporter Kiki, sending you big hugs and hopes for peace across our beautiful Africa! Bye for now!
summary: A special helper from America wants a 'no more guns' rule for all of Sudan to stop fighting, but some big countries in the world's peace club don't agree yet.
whyMatters: This is important because stopping weapons helps stop fighting, which keeps children in Sudan safe so they can go to school, play, and live without fear.

title: Zambia Gets Ready for President's Big Party!
content:
Hello, My Awesome Friends in Africa!

Hi everyone! It's your friendly news reporter, here to share some super exciting news from a very special country in Africa called Zambia. Get ready to hear about a big celebration! We've heard some happy news! People in Zambia are getting ready for a very important day. It's a special party for their President, Mr. Hakainde Hichilema. Everyone is buzzing with excitement!

What is an "Inauguration"?

You might be asking, "What's an inauguration?" Well, it's like a really big, special party. It happens when a President starts his important job. For President Hichilema, it's a celebration because he's starting his important job again, after the people of Zambia chose him to lead once more! Imagine it's your first day of school, or a big birthday party. An inauguration is even bigger! It's when the President promises to take good care of everyone in the country. It's a day full of joy, music, and lots of happy faces. People come together to celebrate their leader and their country. Did you know? The word "inauguration" comes from an old word that means to "begin" something important!

Who is President Hakainde Hichilema?

President Hakainde Hichilema is the leader of Zambia. He's like the head teacher for the whole country! His job is to make sure everyone in Zambia is safe and happy, and that the country grows stronger every day. He works very hard to make sure children can go to school, that there are good doctors, and that everyone has enough food. Being a President is a very big responsibility, and it needs a kind and clever person. Did you know? Zambia is famous for its amazing wildlife, like elephants and zebras, and the incredible Victoria Falls!

Getting Ready for the Big Day!

So, what kind of preparations are happening for President Hichilema's special inauguration? Oh, lots of fun things! Think about getting ready for a huge family party. People are busy planning everything. There will be beautiful decorations everywhere. Imagine colorful flags waving high in the sky! There will probably be bright balloons and flowers to make everything look extra special. There will also be lots of music! African music is so wonderful, with its lively drums and beautiful singing. Everyone will be tapping their feet and clapping their hands. Maybe there will even be some special dances! And what about food? You can bet there will be yummy treats for everyone to enjoy. Inaugurations are often a time for communities to share food and laughter. It's a time when everyone feels proud to be Zambian. People from all over Zambia, and even from other countries, will come to witness this big event. They will dress in their best clothes to celebrate. It's a day for big smiles and happy conversations. Everyone is busy to make sure the celebration is perfect!

Why is This Day So Important?

An inauguration day is very important for a country. It's not just a party; it's a day when everyone remembers that they are one big family. The President promises to lead with care and to help everyone. It shows that Zambia is a strong country. It shows that people believe in their leaders and want to work together for a bright future. It's a day to feel proud of your country and its leaders. It's also a chance for the President to thank everyone for choosing him again. Did you know? In many African countries, special traditional ceremonies are also part of big events like this!

Zambia: A Land of Beauty!

Zambia is a truly amazing country. It's in southern Africa and is known for its friendly people and stunning nature. Imagine wide-open spaces, big rivers, and lots of green trees. It's a place where you can see incredible animals like giraffes, hippos, and many different kinds of birds. The people of Zambia are known for being warm and welcoming. They love to celebrate and share their culture. This inauguration will be another chance for the world to see the beautiful spirit of Zambia and its people. They are getting everything ready to shine brightly on this special day. Did you know? The national bird of Zambia is the African Fish Eagle, which has a very majestic call!

Counting Down to the Celebration!

So, as the preparations continue, everyone in Zambia is looking forward to President Hakainde Hichilema's inauguration. It will be a day to remember, full of joy, pride, and the promise of a wonderful future for Zambia. It's a reminder that even big countries have special moments, just like we have special moments in our lives. Let's all send our warmest wishes to President Hichilema and all the wonderful people of Zambia for a fantastic celebration!
summary: People in Zambia are excitedly getting ready for a special celebration called an inauguration for President Hakainde Hichilema, who is starting his important job again to lead the country.
whyMatters: This is important because it's a big party to celebrate the President starting his job to help everyone in Zambia, showing that the country is strong and happy and ready for a good future.

originalTitle: Root ‘hacked off’ by England cricket team after police handcuff Carse
title: Big News from the World of Cricket!
content:
Hello, Friends! Welcome to Our News!

Hello, amazing friends! It's your kid-friendly news reporter for Africa, bringing you some exciting and important news from around the world. Today, we are going to talk about a super fun game called cricket and learn about some big lessons too! Sometimes, even grown-ups make mistakes, and we can all learn from them. Let's dive in!

What is Cricket? Let's Find Out!

Have you ever seen people playing with a bat and a ball? Cricket is a bit like that! It's a team game played on a big green field. Two teams take turns to bat and score points, called runs. One team tries to hit the ball very far, and the other team tries to catch it and get the players out. It's a game of skill, speed, and lots of teamwork! Did you know? Cricket is played in many countries around the world, including right here in Africa! Countries like South Africa, Kenya, and Zimbabwe have awesome cricket teams.

Meet the England Team!

There's a famous cricket team from a country called England. They play in many big matches against teams from other countries. One of their very important players is the captain. The captain is like the leader of the team. The captain of the England cricket team is a super player named Joe Root. He is very good at hitting the ball and leading his team.

A Big Game Coming Up

Soon, the England team was going to play a very important game. They were going to play against another strong team from a country called Pakistan. These games are called 'Test matches' because they test the players' skills over many days. Everyone was getting ready for this big game. The players practice very hard so they can do their best for their country.

Oh Dear! A Player is Dropped

But then, something big happened! One of the players from the England team, named Brydon Carse, was not going to play in the big game. He was 'dropped' from the team. This means he was told he could not play in the upcoming match. It's usually a very sad thing for a player when this happens.

What Happened? Explaining "Mistakes"

Why was Brydon Carse dropped? Well, Captain Joe Root said that Brydon made some 'stupid mistakes'. These were not small mistakes like dropping a ball during practice. These were big mistakes. Sometimes, when grown-ups make very big mistakes that go against the rules, other grown-ups who help keep everyone safe, like the police, might need to talk to them. Something like this happened with Brydon. The police needed to talk to him because of his mistakes. This is why he could not play in the big game. Did you know? Rules are very important in games and in life. They help us play fair, stay safe, and be kind to each other.

What Does "Dropped" Mean?

When a player is 'dropped', it means they won't be part of the team for a certain game, or maybe even for a while. It's a way for the team to say that the player needs to think about their actions or improve something. It's a way to make sure that everyone on the team follows the rules and behaves responsibly. Even the best players can be dropped if they make big errors.

Captain Joe Root is Not Happy

Captain Joe Root was very upset about the 'stupid mistakes' made by Brydon Carse. He wants all his players to be responsible and follow the rules, both on and off the field. When a captain talks about 'stupid mistakes', it shows he expects everyone to be thoughtful and careful. It's a reminder that everyone needs to be a good example.

Why Rules are Important

This story teaches us an important lesson about rules. Rules are there to help us. They keep us safe and make sure everyone gets along. Whether it's in a game of cricket, in our school, or in our homes, following rules is very important. When we don't follow rules, there can be consequences. Did you know? Good teamwork means everyone follows the rules and helps each other. When one person makes a big mistake, it can affect the whole team.

Learning from Our Mistakes

Even though it's sad that Brydon Carse made mistakes and couldn't play, this is a chance for him to learn. We all make mistakes sometimes, don't we? The important thing is what we do after. We can think about what went wrong, say sorry if we need to, and try our very best not to make the same mistakes again. That's how we grow and become better people.

Cricket in Africa!

It's wonderful to remember that cricket is a game loved by many, including children and grown-ups all over Africa! Maybe one day, you will be a cricket star too, playing for your country! Remember to always play fair, be a good friend, and follow the rules. That's the best way to enjoy any game!

That's All For Today!

Thank you for listening to our news today, my wonderful friends! Always remember to learn from mistakes, be kind, and have fun! See you next time!
summary: England cricket player Brydon Carse was dropped from a big game against Pakistan after making serious mistakes that involved the police, making captain Joe Root very upset.
whyMatters: This news shows us that rules are very important for everyone, even famous sports stars, and that making big mistakes can have consequences, teaching us to always try our best to follow rules and learn from our errors.

originalTitle: China hits out at 'illegal' new US sanctions on Iran and trading partners
title: Friends, Rules, and Oil: A Big Story from Far Away!
content:
Hello from Africa!

Hi, amazing friends in Africa! It’s your friendly news reporter here, so happy to share a story with you today. It’s a story about big countries far away from us. But it helps us understand our wonderful world a little better. We will learn about countries being friends, making rules, and something called oil! Get ready for an exciting adventure of learning with me!

What is 'Doing Business' Between Countries?

Imagine you have a yummy apple. Your friend has a juicy orange. Sometimes, you might swap your apple for their orange, right? That’s a bit like what we mean by 'doing business' or 'trade'. Countries do the same thing, but with much, much bigger things! They buy and sell things like cars, clothes, food, and even special liquids. It helps everyone get what they need and want from other places. **Did you know?** When countries buy and sell things, it's called 'trade'. It helps people all over the world get different kinds of food, toys, and tools!

Meet Iran, the US, and China

Today, we are talking about three big countries in our world. One is called Iran. It’s far away in a place called the Middle East. Another is the United States, which we sometimes just call the US. It’s also very far away, across a big ocean. And the third is China, a giant country in Asia, with so many people! These countries are like big neighbours on our planet Earth. Sometimes they agree on things, and sometimes they don’t quite agree! **Did you know?** China has more people living there than any other country in the world! Imagine how many friends they have!

Why is Oil So Important?

Now, let’s talk about something super important for all of us: oil! Oil is a black, sticky liquid that is found deep, deep under the ground. It might not look very pretty, but it’s like magic because it helps so many things work! We use oil to make our cars, buses, and airplanes go zoom! It also helps make electricity so we can have lights in our homes and watch television. Oil is also used to make many things around us, like plastics and even some clothes! So, many countries need lots and lots of oil every single day. **Did you know?** Oil takes millions of years to form deep inside the Earth! It comes from tiny ancient plants and animals!

When Countries Make Rules for Each Other (Sanctions)

Sometimes, one country might not like something another country is doing. It's a bit like when you have rules at home or at school, to help everyone live and play nicely together. But sometimes, big countries make special rules for other countries. These special rules are called 'sanctions'. They can say things like, 'You can't sell this to that country,' or 'You can't buy that from them.' It’s a way for one country to say, 'Please, we want you to change what you are doing!' **Did you know?** Rules help us stay safe and fair! Even countries have to think about fairness when they make rules.

America's Rules for Iran

The United States (America) has made some new rules for Iran. America says they don't like some things that Iran is doing. So, America has told other countries, 'You should not buy oil from Iran anymore.' They want other countries to stop doing business with Iran, especially about oil. This means America wants to 'isolate' Iran. To 'isolate' means to make a country feel alone, like no one wants to play with them. It's like America is saying, 'If you play with Iran, you can't play with us!' **Did you know?** Countries use rules like this when they want to encourage another country to change its behaviour without having a fight.

China and Iran are Friends (for Business!)

But guess what? Iran has a good friend who buys lots and lots of its oil! This friend is China! China is a very big country and needs lots of oil for its cars, big factories, and homes. And Iran has lots of oil that it wants to sell. So, China and Iran have been doing business together for a long, long time. They help each other by buying and selling this important black liquid. It's a very important business friendship for both countries, helping their people. **Did you know?** China is one of the biggest buyers of oil in the world! They need a lot of energy to keep their country running!

China Says 'No Thank You!' to America's Rules

Now, America has told everyone, 'Stop buying oil from Iran!' But China heard this and said, 'Hold on a minute! We don't like these rules!' China thinks it's not fair for America to tell them who they can buy oil from. China wants to keep buying oil from Iran because it helps their people get what they need. They believe it is their right to choose their own friends and business partners. So, China is saying, 'No thank you, America, we will keep doing business with Iran!' It’s a big disagreement between these two very powerful countries in the world. **Did you know?** Countries often talk a lot to try and find a way to agree, even when they have big differences. Talking is very important!

Why This Matters (Even for Us!)

You might be thinking, 'Why does this big story matter to me, a child in Africa?' Well, when big countries like America and China talk about rules for important things like oil, it can affect everyone. If it’s harder to buy oil, then oil might become more expensive to buy. When oil is expensive, it costs more to make cars and buses go. It can also cost more to make things in factories that use oil to work. And sometimes, even the food or toys you buy in the shops might cost more too. So, even though it's happening far away, it reminds us that our world is connected, like a big family! **Did you know?** The price of oil can affect how much your favourite toys or even fresh food might cost, because transporting them from far away uses oil!

Let's Learn More Every Day!

Wow, that was a big story for today, my clever friends! We learned about countries, doing business, important oil, and special rules. It's amazing how much there is to discover about our wonderful world. Keep being curious and always ask questions, because that’s how we all learn and grow stronger and smarter. I’m so proud of you for listening and learning today! See you next time with more exciting news from our big, beautiful world!
summary: Big countries called America and China are talking about new rules for another country called Iran, especially about selling important oil.
whyMatters: When big countries talk about rules for important things like oil, it can make it harder for everyone to buy and sell things, and sometimes prices can go up, affecting us too!
